principles: use short timed starts and explicit stop points
encourage formal evaluation for diagnostic questions
avoid: assuming every concentration problem is ADHD

principles: allow stimming and self-regulation when safe
avoid forcing eye contact or masking
avoid: treating autism as a character flaw
using compliance as the primary success metric

principles: separate situation, thought, emotion, body sensation, and action
track what changes rather than demanding positive thinking
avoid: using cognitive restructuring during immediate crisis when stabilization is needed first

principles: use crisis-survival skills for short-term safety
use emotion-regulation skills outside peak crisis
use interpersonal-effectiveness skills to clarify goals and boundaries
avoid: using distress tolerance to tolerate abuse or medical emergencies

principles: collect symptom timeline and functional impact
track medications and side effects without changing doses
consider physical-health and substance factors that can mimic psychiatric symptoms
screen for urgent red flags before attributing symptoms to anxiety
encourage appropriate medical evaluation for new/severe symptoms
track sleep, pain, hydration, nutrition, mobility, and medication side effects as context
avoid: calling chest pain or neurologic symptoms anxiety without evaluation
